newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Summer crop prospects shine in NSW Australia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Summer crop prospects shine in NSW Australia.

text.p: Summer crop prospects in the Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) were excellent, with sowings estimated at 256,000 hectares against 237,000 ha harvested last season, the New South Wales Department of Agriculture said a state grain report.
This excluded cotton and rice, the department said.
Following favourable seasonal conditions, especially in December, crops established satisfactorily, it said.
Dryland crops needed rain to secure the excellent prospects, it said.
Sorghum sowings were estimated at 143,000 ha, maize at 29,000 ha, mungbean at 12,000, soybean at 26,000 ha and sunflower at 43,000 ha.

Among winter crops, overall wheat grain quality was excellent with a good proportion of the crop delivered as Prime Hard. Exceptionally large quantities of Australian Hard were produced in all areas, it said.
Record average yields of barley also were havested, with a large quantity of malting grade delivered from all areas, it said.
